deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let pi be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} (Grothendieck's pi-hat_{0,3}). It is free profinite on l_0 and l_1, with inertia generators satisfying l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1. The group S_3 of automorphisms of P^1 permuting 0, 1, infinity acts on this space. This gives an extension 1 -> pi -> E -> S_3 -> 1, which embeds in Aut(pi) because pi has trivial centre. The involutions sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf lift the transpositions fixing 0, 1, infinity respectively. rho is a lift of the 3-cycle. Gamma = Autext_loc(pi, S_3) is the group of outer automorphisms that respect the inertia classes and commute with S_3. It is the 1981 precursor of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.

Previous page. An element u of Gamma is normalised by u(l_0) = l_0^chi and u(L_1) = int(g)(L_1). This gives invariants chi (the cyclotomic-type character, in Z-hat^*) and gamma(u) = class of g modulo the action phi(alpha): g -> l_0^alpha g l_1^-alpha. The pair (gamma, chi) is claimed to be injective on Gamma.

This page, top lines. Commutation with sigma_inf (which swaps 0 and 1) imposes sigma_inf(g^-1) = l_0^beta g l_1^beta, and the text asserts that this determines beta uniquely from g. Check by abelianising: if g^ab = a l_0 + b l_1, then sigma_inf swaps the two coordinates. The relation reads -(b,a) = (a+beta, b+beta), so beta = -(a+b). Hence beta is forced by g^ab and is invariant under phi. After normalisation, this is the analogue of the Drinfeld/Ihara 'two-cycle' relation f(y,x) = f(x,y)^-1 for GT.

Crossed-out paragraph. An attempt to apply the 'fundamental relation' u rho = int(g) rho u to the decomposition/inertia subgroup L_0. Using u(L_0) = L_0 and rho(L_0) = L_1 one gets u(L_1) = int(g)(L_1). So g is determined only up to a double coset (left by L_0, right by L_1), i.e. an element of L_0 \ pi / L_1. It is abandoned.

Main new idea. Find nicer generators for E than the six elements l_0, l_1, l_inf, sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf (with rho = sigma_0 sigma_1 up to an inertia factor). In the quotient orbifold (P^1 minus 3 points)/S_3, the three cusps 0, 1, infinity map to one point. Its 'ramification group' is a copy of Z-hat containing the inertia l_i with index 2, and the three are canonically isomorphic. So one defines eps_i, the unique element in the coset sigma_i * pi that fixes l_i and satisfies eps_i^2 = l_i.

Modern reading. P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} is the lambda-line Y(2) and S_3 = PSL_2(Z)/Gamma(2)-bar. So E is the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3, i.e. of B_3/centre. The eps_i are the three parabolic elements (conjugates of T = [[1,1],[0,1]]) at the cusps of Gamma(2), and eps_i^2 = l_i is the statement that T^2 generates the cusp stabiliser of Gamma(2). The next page computes eps_inf = l_0 sigma_inf l_inf, eps_0 = l_1 sigma_0 l_0 and eps_1 = l_inf sigma_1 l_1 (after testing alpha = 1).
errors: The phrase 'donnant rho par sigma_0 sigma_1 = l_1 rho près, i.e. rho = sigma_0 sigma_1 l_1 près' is sloppy: sigma_0 sigma_1 = l_1 rho gives rho = l_1^-1 sigma_0 sigma_1. The 'près' (up to an inertia factor) makes this harmless.
The uniqueness of beta is asserted without proof. It is correct: abelianisation gives beta = -(a+b), where (a,b) are the exponent sums of g in l_0 and l_1.

Existence of eps_i with eps_i^2 = l_i is not automatic for an arbitrary lift sigma_i. The next page shows that a correcting factor int(l_inf^alpha) with alpha = 1 is needed, after a first guess fails.

ideas.what: Group Autext_loc(pi_{0,3}, S_3) of inertia-preserving outer automorphisms commuting with S_3, parametrised by (gamma, chi) with g in pi modulo the twist g -> l_0^a g l_1^-a
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT-hat (pairs (lambda, f)), first relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) describes the Teichmüller tower programme, but not this explicit parametrisation

ideas.what: Relation sigma_inf(g^-1) = l_0^beta g l_1^beta with beta forced by g
ideas.modern_name: two-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 of GT (up to normalisation)

ideas.what: Extension of S_3 by pi inside Aut(pi), with canonical square roots eps_i of the inertia generators coming from the cusp 'ramification groups' Z-hat
ideas.modern_name: profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = B_3/Z containing Gamma(2)-hat; parabolic elements T with T^2 in Gamma(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (PSL_2(Z) / Gamma(2)); its use for GT in Lochak-Schneps, Ihara, Nakamura 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} and the Galois action on them, but not these generators

missed.claim: Already in spring 1981, Grothendieck defines a group Gamma of S_3-equivariant inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of pi-hat_{0,3}. He parametrises it injectively by (cyclotomic-type character, class of g) and extracts the GT-type symmetry relation, nine years before Drinfeld's GT-hat. This is known in outline from the Esquisse, but the explicit relations are not in print under his name.
missed.quote: sigma_inf(g^-1) = l_0^beta g l_1^beta. Ce qui détermine beta de façon unique en fonction de g.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority and a record of how the GT relations first emerged. The S_3 / PSL_2(Z)-hat-extension viewpoint gives an alternative presentation of GT-hat.

missed.claim: Passing to the 'ramification groups' at 0, 1, infinity, which are all canonically Z-hat, implicitly identifies the S_3-extension of pi-hat_{0,3} with PSL_2(Z)-hat (the j-line orbifold). The square-root generators eps_i are the cusp parabolics. This links the genus-0, 3-point analysis to M_{1,1} at the level of explicit generators.
missed.quote: les groupes de ramification dans les pts 0,1,inf, qui sont canoniquement isomorphes : Z-hat ... eps_0^2 = l_0, eps_1^2 = l_1, eps_inf^2 = l_inf
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the same mechanism later used (Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura) to let GT-hat act on B_3-hat / PSL_2(Z)-hat. It is likely known to specialists, so its novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early, explicit proto-GT computation (symmetry relation, square roots of inertia in the S_3-extension). It is historically interesting but mathematically subsumed by Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak-Schneps, and Grothendieck's 1981 interest in this group is broadly known.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le demi-tore R des sigma_i' is doubtful. More likely 'dans la classe (mod pi) des sigma_i' or similar: eps_i must lie in the coset of sigma_i over the transposition fixing i.

The crossed-out passage 'une double multiplication à droite par un élément de L_1' probably refers to a double coset (left by L_0, right by L_1), i.e. g determined modulo L_0 \ pi / L_1. 'sur le domaine de u' may be 'sur le choix de u'.

The insertion over 'générateurs' reads '{+son+}' / 'l'extension'. The intended sense is 'de plus jolis générateurs de l'extension de S_3 par pi dans Aut(pi)': the transcription's 'Aut_ext(pi)' should probably be 'Aut(pi)' or 'Aut_loc(pi)'.
